title: Teams app manifest 1.30 that packages a declarative agent
summary: Microsoft 365 app manifest 1.30 with copilotAgents.declarativeAgents that wraps a declarative agent manifest into an installable package, including limits, layout and rollout steps.
body:
The app manifest that turns a declarative agent into an installable Microsoft 365 app. The agent itself lives in declarativeAgent.json; the app manifest (version 1.30, the newest version listed on Microsoft Learn when this entry was written) only describes the package and points to the agent through copilotAgents.declarativeAgents, which takes exactly one item with an id and a relative file path. Use it together with the HR benefits manifest entry of this library.

=== File: manifest.json ===
Comment: required root properties are manifestVersion, version, id, developer, name, description, icons and accentColor. Limits: developer.name 32 characters, name.short 30, name.full 100, description.short 80, description.full 4000, packageName 64; short and full values must differ. declarativeAgents has a minimum and maximum of one item. file is a path inside the package, at most 2048 characters. validDomains must list the domains of card links and images that the agent's plugins render.
{
 "$schema": "https://developer.microsoft.com/json-schemas/teams/v1.30/MicrosoftTeams.schema.json",
 "manifestVersion": "1.30",
 "version": "1.0.0",
 "id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",
 "packageName": "example.contoso.hrassistant",
 "developer": {
  "name": "Contoso HR IT",
  "websiteUrl": "https://contoso.example",
  "privacyUrl": "https://contoso.example/privacy",
  "termsOfUseUrl": "https://contoso.example/terms"
 },
 "name": {
  "short": "HR Assistant",
  "full": "Contoso HR Benefits Assistant"
 },
 "description": {
  "short": "Answers HR benefits and leave questions in Copilot.",
  "full": "The Contoso HR Benefits Assistant is an agent for Microsoft 365 Copilot. It answers questions about benefits, leave and onboarding from approved HR policies in SharePoint and shows where each answer comes from. No external account is required."
 },
 "icons": {
  "outline": "outline.png",
  "color": "color.png"
 },
 "accentColor": "#0F6CBD",
 "copilotAgents": {
  "declarativeAgents": [
   {
    "id": "hrAssistant",
    "file": "declarativeAgent.json"
   }
  ]
 },
 "validDomains": [
  "contoso.sharepoint.example"
 ]
}

=== Package layout (text) ===
Comment: zip the files without a parent folder.
appPackage/
  manifest.json
  declarativeAgent.json
  color.png        (192 x 192, full colour)
  outline.png      (32 x 32, transparent, white outline)

=== How to use ===
1. Generate a new GUID for id and keep it stable for the life of the app; do not reuse the placeholder.
2. Increase version on every update; every change to the package requires a higher version.
3. Make sure description.full states whether an external account is required, and keep description.short out of the full text.
4. Create the zip and test it by uploading the custom app in Teams or the Microsoft 365 admin center, then open Copilot and pick the agent.
5. For organization-wide rollout, upload the package in the Microsoft 365 admin center and assign it to users or groups.

=== Common mistakes ===
- Making name.short and name.full identical; they must differ.
- Using http URLs for developer links; the schema expects http or https, but production apps should use https.
- Referencing a declarative agent file that is not inside the zip, or putting a folder level around the files.
- Adding a second declarativeAgents item. The array allows exactly one.
- Skipping validDomains when plugins return cards with images or links; Copilot will not render images from unlisted domains.

title: Teams app manifest 1.30 for a personal tab and channel tab with Entra single sign-on
summary: App manifest 1.30 with a pinned personal tab, a configurable tab for channels and chats, webApplicationInfo for single sign-on, validDomains and install scope settings.
body:
A classic tab app: one static (personal) tab that is pinned in the app, and one configurable tab that users add to a team channel, group chat or meeting chat after a configuration page. Entra single sign-on is declared with webApplicationInfo, and validDomains lists the host of the tab pages. App manifest 1.30. staticTabs currently supports the personal scope only, a configurable tab is not supported in the personal scope, and only one configurable tab per app is allowed. All URLs, GUIDs and the Entra resource URI are placeholders.

=== File: manifest.json ===
Comment: required root properties are manifestVersion, version, id, developer, name, description, icons and accentColor. Limits: developer.name 32 characters, name.short 30, name.full 100, description.short 80, description.full 4000, packageName 64; short and full values must differ. staticTabs: entityId is required (64 characters), scopes is required, contentUrl is a URL of at most 2048 characters. configurableTabs: configurationUrl and scopes are required, scopes allows team and groupChat, at most two values.
{
 "$schema": "https://developer.microsoft.com/json-schemas/teams/v1.30/MicrosoftTeams.schema.json",
 "manifestVersion": "1.30",
 "version": "1.0.0",
 "id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",
 "packageName": "example.contoso.projectboard",
 "developer": {
  "name": "Contoso Apps",
  "websiteUrl": "https://contoso.example",
  "privacyUrl": "https://contoso.example/privacy",
  "termsOfUseUrl": "https://contoso.example/terms"
 },
 "name": {
  "short": "Project Board",
  "full": "Contoso Project Board"
 },
 "description": {
  "short": "Personal dashboard and channel tab for project boards.",
  "full": "Project Board gives you a personal overview of your tasks and lets teams add a shared board as a tab in a channel or group chat. Sign-in uses your Microsoft work account through single sign-on."
 },
 "icons": {
  "outline": "outline.png",
  "color": "color.png"
 },
 "accentColor": "#2564CF",
 "staticTabs": [
  {
   "entityId": "myTasks",
   "name": "My tasks",
   "scopes": [
    "personal"
   ],
   "context": [
    "personalTab"
   ],
   "contentUrl": "https://board.contoso.example/personal",
   "websiteUrl": "https://board.contoso.example/personal"
  }
 ],
 "configurableTabs": [
  {
   "id": "boardTab",
   "configurationUrl": "https://board.contoso.example/configure",
   "canUpdateConfiguration": true,
   "scopes": [
    "team",
    "groupChat"
   ],
   "context": [
    "channelTab",
    "privateChatTab",
    "meetingChatTab"
   ],
   "supportedPlatform": [
    "desktop",
    "mobile"
   ]
  }
 ],
 "defaultInstallScope": "personal",
 "supportedChannelTypes": [
  "sharedChannels"
 ],
 "validDomains": [
  "board.contoso.example"
 ],
 "webApplicationInfo": {
  "id": "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111",
  "resource": "api://board.contoso.example/11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111"
 }
}

=== How to use ===
1. Create the Microsoft Entra app registration for SSO: expose an API with the application ID URI that matches webApplicationInfo.resource and authorize the Teams client applications; put the app (client) ID into webApplicationInfo.id.
2. Build the pages for contentUrl and configurationUrl; the configuration page calls the Teams JavaScript library to save the tab settings.
3. Add all hosts that the pages load content from to validDomains. The domain of contentUrl is trusted automatically, but add any other host you use.
4. Package, upload as a custom app and test the personal tab, then add the configurable tab in a channel, a group chat and a meeting chat.
5. If you do not use SSO, remove webApplicationInfo or use a harmless dummy value on a domain you control.

=== Common mistakes ===
- Using the personal scope on a configurable tab; it is not supported.
- Declaring two configurable tabs. The array allows one.
- Listing overly broad wildcard domains such as *.com in validDomains. Use exact host names, or a subdomain wildcard such as *.contoso.example for a domain you control.
- Using an application ID URI that does not match webApplicationInfo.resource, which breaks the token request.
- Forgetting to increase version after you change tab URLs or scopes.
